title: Refusing Oliver's New York trip and staying in California
summary: Oliver announced the move to New York; Garland stayed in California for his woman, good job and the weather, then received a ticket after Oliver left.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well, I was playing myself, uh, everybody but, uh, Jolly Roll's band played. Jolly Roll Morton played with us. We went there to play with Jolly Roll for two nights. I see. He'd give a dance out to this place. Uh-huh. He'd run the place. He'd give dances out there all the time. Holidays and all sadness and Sundays. Yeah. And we went down to the play. So when they finished those two nights, Joe said, Well, we're going to New York. Who said that?
Uh-huh. He's going to leave, I think, on a Monday or something. When? When? When? When?
He's not doing that week. Get ready, boys. We're going to New York. I said, Well, Joe, I'm sorry. I ain't going no further.

Because I didn't meet Oren now. You see, Oren was in Oakland. He's butt. See? And they was waiting on 11 in, uh, Broadway, a little cafe there. Five of them. I told him I'd come back. He said, Well, uh, why? I said, Well, I think I'll have to stay out here. I ain't going no further. I got you a corner woman now. You don't want to go no further, huh? You don't have to be a native.
Because you got your corner and you got you a good woman now.

I said, No. I ain't going back there. I said, I can get my shoe shined the whole year around. I said, California. I can't get my shoe shined back there in New York in the winter. I said, I'm tired. Tired of walking all that snow. I ain't got flying. I got all situated. I know I'm going right on the job, you see. I said, Well, I come back that night. Let's go over the show. We live right there. I live in lovely Southern. And the show right across the street from there, the Hub's Theater. Let's go over the show. I said, I don't feel that kind of way. Man, what's the matter with you? I'm going to go back to New York and get on a good job. I said, Sure, I ain't going back to New York. My mama sat here a while. He couldn't get me to go. He cussed me out, you know. I said, Okay, pal. So he sat. We was in Oakland. So finally he set a telegram for me to come, yeah, to New York. I told him, Yeah. I said, All right.

And he sent me a ticket. This is after he went to New York? After he went back, yeah. He sent it for me. That's when he had this big band we were going to have down there and all that bunch of plays for him. He sent it for me. I goes to work like a fool and so much to do the bank.
